content.user_title: Plan Coding Work With Structured Decisions
content.value_statement: Teams often start coding before requirements, scope, and tradeoffs are clear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured planning and prioritization.
actual_capabilities: Guides requirement questioning before coding starts.
Uses a 5-step framework to remove, simplify, accelerate, and automate work.
Applies ICE scoring to compare feature and refactor options.
Provides planning checklists for features, refactors, and testing setup.
Highlights red flags such as unclear estimates, weak typing, and oversized components.
limitations: Does not execute plans or modify code by itself.
Does not replace product requirements or stakeholder approval.
Uses examples from one project, so teams must adapt details.
May mention package-management commands that require user review.

use_cases.title: Feature Planning
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into requirements, tradeoffs, priority, and a short implementation plan.

use_cases.title: Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Compare implementation approaches before committing to dependencies, state management, or automation.

use_cases.title: Refactor Prioritization
use_cases.description: Decide which cleanup work matters now and which work should remain in the backlog.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one scoped change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [feature] using this framework. Question the requirement, identify deletions, compare options with ICE scoring, and produce a short implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [approach A] and [approach B]. Use impact, confidence, and ease scores, then recommend the simpler option with risks.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this refactor idea: [description]. Identify what to delete, what to extract, what to defer, and what tests reduce risk.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Full Delivery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a delivery plan for [project]. Include requirement questions, ICE scores, file impact, staged increments, edge cases, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Plan an export button for a metrics table.
output: Questioned whether users need spreadsheets or a simpler CSV export.
Recommended one export action in the existing table toolbar.
Estimated high impact, high confidence, and moderate effort.

output_examples.input: Decide whether to add a new charting library.
output: Checked whether the current library can handle the requirement.
Flagged dependency size and migration cost as decision risks.
Recommended testing the smallest proof of concept before adoption.

output_examples.input: Plan a refactor for a large component.
output: Identified extraction candidates for state, chart display, and statistics.
Deferred unrelated UI changes to keep scope controlled.
Listed regression tests for the existing behavior.

best_practices: Question the requirement before comparing implementation options.
Delete unnecessary scope before optimizing the remaining design.
Use ICE scores as a discussion aid, not as the only decision rule.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation before defining the real problem.
Adding dependencies before checking simpler existing options.
Treating early time estimates as reliable without risk review.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan coding work before implementation. It focuses on requirements, scope, tradeoffs, priority, and validation.

faq.question: Can it write code for me?
faq.answer: The skill is for planning. Claude, Codex, or Claude Code may implement later using the plan you approve.

faq.question: What is ICE scoring?
faq.answer: ICE scoring compares impact, confidence, and ease. It helps rank features, refactors, and technical tasks.

faq.question: Is it only for large projects?
faq.answer: No. It works best for changes with meaningful uncertainty, multiple options, or more than a small edit.

faq.question: Does it require special tools?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown planning guide for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should teams use the output?
faq.answer: Review the plan, adjust assumptions, then implement the smallest testable increment first.
